title: Parvez v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: V.K. Shukla and Shashi Kant, JJ.
docket: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 15887 of 2014
disposition: FIR quash refused; CrPC 41/41-A directed if arrest made; compounding left to Supply Code 2005.
headnote: An FIR under ss.135/138 of the Electricity Act, 2003 that discloses a cognizable offence is not quashed. If arrest is to be made and the offence cannot attract a sentence exceeding seven years, the police must follow CrPC ss.41(1)(b) and 41-A. If the offence is compoundable, compounding is to be sought under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Parvez petitioned the Allahabad High Court to quash an FIR dated 17 August 2014, Case Crime No. 240 of 2014, registered at Police Station Behat, District Saharanpur, under sections 135/138 of the Electricity Act, 2003. He had not been arrested. Counsel argued that the alleged offence could not attract a sentence of more than seven years, so arrest should not be mechanical, and that the offence was compoundable. The A.G.A. appeared for the State; counsel for opposite party no. 4 was present.

holding_units.topic: quashing of theft FIR; arrest and compounding
holding_units.holding: An FIR under sections 135/138 of the Electricity Act, 2003 that discloses a cognizable offence will not be quashed. Where arrest has not yet been made and the offence cannot entail a sentence of more than seven years, any arrest must comply with section 41(1)(b) read with section 41-A CrPC. If the offence is compoundable, the accused may seek compounding under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

principle_tags.application: Applied where a s.135/138 FIR was left standing: arrest, if at all, must follow CrPC 41/41-A, and compounding is for the Supply Code 2005, not the writ.

not_decided.point: Whether the alleged s.135/138 offence was in fact compoundable on these facts
not_decided.note: Court said only that if the offence is compoundable, the petitioner may seek the Supply Code 2005 remedy.
